terra.problem: The joke compares Jesus being noticed to Papa’s nose detecting cookies. Comparisons and humor must stay on the human side, not make Jesus the subject of the joke.
The bakery comparison makes Jesus’ visit and His inability to escape notice the subject of the joke.
Mark says the woman came and fell at Jesus’ feet, but does not say whether she hung back or sent anyone ahead.
Saying there was no waiting at the door rules out a detail the text does not address.
The woman does not say that nobody is put off until later. Her answer leaves that detail open.
The explanation repeats the answer and ends with the flat definition, “Begging is serious asking.”
“Just Jesus and the man” asserts that nobody else was there. Mark says Jesus took him away from the crowd, not that the two were alone.
“The crowd stayed back” describes what the crowd did, which Mark does not say.
“Hands aren’t in this scene” overlooks Jesus putting His fingers into the man’s ears.
“One word and nothing else” rules out other speech the text does not address. The passage also says the tongue was released, not that it needed opening.

“The louder the news got” changes Mark’s point. He says they proclaimed it more widely, not more loudly.
“It didn’t stay quiet for any stretch” adds a timing detail Mark does not give.
“Far past the family dinner table” adds details about whom the people told. Mark says they proclaimed it more widely.
